### 8.4 Branch-structure options

**Git constraint (applies to every layout that uses a slash).** `feat/review-panel` and `feat/review-panel/<name>` cannot both exist: a ref name cannot be both a branch and a directory of branches, because git stores `refs/heads/feat/review-panel` as a file and `refs/heads/feat/review-panel/<name>` needs a directory of the same name. A layout therefore either has an umbrella branch `feat/review-panel` with children named without a slash after `review-panel` (for example `feat/review-panel-m1-core`), or has namespaced children `feat/review-panel/<name>` with no branch called `feat/review-panel`.

**Facts that shape the options** (all from the research files; ownership is owner item O-4, G-92): the `cli/review` package on this branch equals `origin/master`, so the E1 kernel is master code after #519 and the branch `ironbelly/shadow-runs` is 3 commits ahead of `origin/master` touching only `SKILL.md`, `refs/reviewer-spec.md`, two reflect tests and documents (`research/09` section 1.1; GQ:D-72); the local `master` ref is stale, so any new branch is cut from `origin/master` (project rule: fetch and rebase onto `origin/master` before pushing); PRs go only to the fork `IronbellyOrg/IronClaude` through `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3`, never to the upstream; worktrees are created through Orca with an agent; `.claude/` mirrors are never staged and `.dev/tasks/` is always staged; the reflect pins C1, C6, C14 compare with HEAD, so changes to the reflect skill text are kept in separate commits from changes to the pinned sections and G8 is run before each commit; the live7 test couples `review-tiers.default.json` to `ccsession-models.json`, so tier edits and that file change in one PR (GQ:G-90); both panel goldens regenerate on any tier-file byte change, so two branches that edit the tier file or the resolution record conflict. The rollback unit in every layout is one merged PR, so layouts C and D revert all the steps they merged together (the rollback lines of 8.2 and the persisted-format rule of the M1 intro apply). This section states layouts and trade-offs only; it commits to no order, date or sprint.

| Option | Branch layout | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Flat sibling branches, no umbrella | One branch per track or per group of steps cut from `origin/master`, named without a slash after `review-panel`: `feat/review-panel-m1-contract`, `feat/review-panel-m1-resolver`, `feat/review-panel-m2-reflect`, `feat/review-panel-m3-post-gate`, `feat/review-panel-m4-pr`; each PR targets master directly | Satisfies the git constraint trivially; each PR is reviewed and gated alone (G-all green per PR); matches the "branch from master, PR to the fork" rule; M3 post-gate repairs (code-only, G9) do not wait on M1 | Shared files (`findings_v2.py`, `panel.py`, both goldens, `test_review_cluster.py:784-795`) conflict between siblings; reviewers see a half-unified core between merges; cross-track dependencies (M2 on M1-02, M1-06, M1-09) need the earlier PR merged or a stacked rebase |
| B. Namespaced children, no `feat/review-panel` branch | `feat/review-panel/m1-contract`, `feat/review-panel/m1-resolver`, `feat/review-panel/m2-reflect`, `feat/review-panel/m3-post-gate`, `feat/review-panel/m4-pr`, each cut from `origin/master`; no branch is named `feat/review-panel` | Groups the work in branch listings and Orca; same per-PR gating as A; the slash form is allowed because no branch has the parent name | Cannot later create an umbrella `feat/review-panel` without deleting all children first (the constraint bites at that point); same conflict and dependency costs as A; some tooling lists namespaced branches awkwardly |
| C. Umbrella integration branch with flat children | Umbrella `feat/review-panel` cut from `origin/master`; children named `feat/review-panel-<name>` (not `feat/review-panel/<name>`) PR into the umbrella; the umbrella merges to master through `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3` once G-all, G-exit and the track's acceptance checks pass | Master only ever sees a coherent core; golden regeneration and pin changes (C1/C6/C14, `test_review_cluster.py:784-795`) land once; children can be reviewed small | A long-lived umbrella drifts from master (rebase onto `origin/master` before every push); one large final PR is harder to review and to bisect; the HEAD-relative pins protect only uncommitted edits, so a long branch hides contract drift between commits unless M2-01 (absolute pin) lands first; the fork-only PR rule applies to the umbrella and to every child PR |
| D. Single branch for the whole programme | One branch `feat/review-panel` holding all tracks, one PR | Simplest to create; no cross-branch conflicts | Violates the "small reviewable change" intent; the four debates left HIGH invariants open, so one PR would carry undecided design (C03, C05, C13, C14) and could not be merged in parts; M3 Critical repairs (false-green post gate) would wait on unrelated tracks; hardest to roll back |
| E. Keep `ironbelly/shadow-runs` for reflect only, core on separate branches | Continue the existing branch (M2 work and the shadow-run evidence) and cut the M1 core and M3/M4 work onto new flat or namespaced branches from `origin/master` | Preserves the shadow-run history and the evidence documents (`.dev/tasks/` stays staged); no rename of a branch that other worktrees use | Two lineages touch `sc-reflect-protocol/SKILL.md` and the pinned tests, so C1/C6/C14 runs must be repeated on each; the shared kernel is on master already, so M2 steps that need new M1 pieces must wait for those PRs (a dependency, not an order); the branch is 3 commits ahead of `origin/master`, so it must be rebased before any push |

## 9. Open Questions

**Source key.** `Gnn` = gap row nn of `gaps-and-questions.md` section 1; `Dnn` = row nn of its section 2; `Onn` = owner item of its section 3; `Cnn` = closed item of its section 4. `NN` = `research/NN-*.md`. Effort tags: E1 = reflect Tier 2 panel and shadow mode (branch `ironbelly/shadow-runs`); E2 = tasklist review-panel evaluation study at the E2 commit above; E3 = #346 review loop on master plus installed-only experiment variants. Closure effort: C1 = no new work (the report carries it from existing evidence), C2 = small read-only check, C3 = new research, a measured run or an input only the owner or another session can supply.

**Severity.** Under the gap-log rating no gap is Critical (both cross-validation and both gap-detection reports state that none blocks synthesis). 30 gaps are Important; all 30 appear below as their own question or as a named part of one (rows Q-01 to Q-30). All 64 Minor gaps appear in rows Q-05, Q-02 or Q-31 to Q-44.

Gap-log rating: 94 gaps, 0 Critical, 30 Important, 64 Minor. Section 4 re-rates 15 rows Critical and 66 Important (the 15 Critical rows are 11 distinct gaps: 7 under control C8, 4 on impact, see Section 4.1 row 15); both counts are used, each with its basis, and Section 9 follows the gap-log rating.

Row labels: [Required] = a question the task requires in this table; [Owner] = from AMBIGUITIES_FOR_USER; [Important] = an Important gap not already listed; [Minor group] = Minor gaps grouped by theme (each gap ID named); [Web] = an UNVERIFIED item from the web research files; [Debate] = an open decision or unaddressed invariant left by one of the four adversarial debates or by the QA gate (rows Q-47 to Q-61, Section 9.5; these rows carry no gap ID). A gap that appears in a [Required] row is not repeated elsewhere. Section 9.1 maps every gap ID to its question row.
